claims.text: The low hardness and strength of single-phase equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are primarily governed by dynamic recovery during deformation.
Dislocations have high mobility in the homogeneous CoCrFeNiTi solid solution.
High dislocation mobility causes rapid dislocation annihilation in this alloy.
Rapid dislocation annihilation prevents the buildup of the dislocation density that would otherwise strengthen the alloy.
The applicable starting material is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution structure.
Reduced testing temperature restricts dynamic recovery relative to room-temperature testing.
High strain-rate deformation restricts dynamic recovery relative to low strain-rate deformation.
Low strain-rate deformation promotes dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery is governed by the balance between dislocation accumulation and annihilation in the absence of significant secondary-phase precipitates.
During deformation, mobile dislocations rapidly rearrange and annihilate through dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery limits dislocation interactions required for strain hardening.
Limited strain hardening caused by dynamic recovery produces relatively low hardness and strength.
Dynamic recovery helps maintain favorable plasticity and machinability.
Deformation at lower temperatures and higher strain rates should produce a higher dislocation density than deformation at room temperature and low strain rates.
Conditions that inhibit dynamic recovery should produce higher hardness than conditions that favor recovery.
Conditions that inhibit dynamic recovery should produce higher yield strength than conditions that favor recovery.
The proposed mechanism applies only where phase separation or second-phase precipitation does not dominate deformation behavior.
